recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR-31784. Treat future changes from the DeviceDefinition canonical-resource issue family separately because they concern reference typing, not this cardinality decision.
issue_request: FHIR-31784 asked how an AdministrableProductDefinition could have multiple integral devices for one substance and form. The Published/Persuasive resolution changed AdministrableProductDefinition.device cardinality to 0..1 because no examples supporting multiple devices were found.
initial_application: The change was applied before this reconciliation: 2021-09-14 git commits titled "just one device per administrable product FHIR#31784" changed the source element max from * to 1, and the Jira comments say the change was applied in both the R4B branch and main build.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively includes AdministrableProductDefinition and maps the resource folder, confirming the checked XML is in build scope. The current source and combined branch still have AdministrableProductDefinition.device at max 1. BR&R 2021-08-17 minutes list FHIR-31784 among ballot reconciliation tickets and point detailed resolutions back to Jira. FHIR-39389 later mentions AdministrableProductDefinition.device only in a broader, not-yet-Applied DeviceDefinition canonical-reference migration, not as a cardinality change.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The published empty audit commit records that the current source already matches the FHIR-31784 resolution.

related_jiras.note: Later DeviceDefinition canonical-resource issue mentions AdministrableProductDefinition.device as a possible reference-type migration, but it is not Applied/Published and does not revisit the 0..1 cardinality.
